asinine

AS-ih-nyn · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Asinine is extremely stupid -- so senseless it invites scorn.

Skipping the safety briefing before the hike was an asinine decision that could have ended badly.

Example

Forgetting to check the weather before the sailing trip turned out to be a truly asinine oversight, one that nearly capsized the boat.

Asinine describes a decision or comment so senseless it seems almost intentionally stupid -- stronger and more dismissive than simply calling something a mistake.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

foolish: Foolish is the everyday word for lacking good sense, and it stretches from small slips to big blunders. Asinine sits at the harsh far end of that range: it brands an act extremely stupid, almost insultingly so, where foolish can stay gentle.

idiotic: Idiotic is a harsh word for something extremely unwise, close in force to asinine. The difference is flavor: asinine adds a sneer of contempt, suggesting the blunder was so senseless it seems almost intentional, while idiotic is blunt name-calling without that edge.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

sensible: showing good sense

wise: showing sound judgment

Where it sits · how deep the stupidity runs — silly → asinine → moronic

silly vs. asinine: A silly mistake -- mismatched socks, a mispronounced name -- is only a little embarrassing, nowhere near the deep stupidity that asinine accuses someone of.

moronic vs. asinine: Moronic goes a step further than asinine: both brand an act extremely stupid, but moronic pushes the insult to the very bottom of the scale.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Asinine comes from the Latin word asinus, referring to a donkey -- describing behavior as stubborn or foolish as a work animal, though the root doesn't survive in any other common modern English word.

Use the root in a new word: asinus

Use the root in a new word: asinus: The Latin root asinus is also the direct ancestor of the everyday farm-animal word for a donkey -- the two words share the exact same origin.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Asinine is a blunt, dismissive word -- it works well venting frustration about a foolish decision, but it can come across as harsh or insulting if aimed directly at a person.
